mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) substantially exceeds its all-prior average AND the opponent's shots AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR) substantially exceeds competition context, then examine whether the corner-kick FOR rate and shots-on-target FOR rate move together or diverge relative to the goals FOR rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume surges above its own baseline AND the opponent structurally allows many shots, corner-kick generation rises with shot volume but goals FOR rises less than proportionally, indicating a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and conversion in this joint condition.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is jointly elevated in recent form (shots FOR rising sharply) while Team B concedes shots at a level well above competition context, but Team B's shots-on-target allowed has not risen proportionally in recent form — suggesting a divergence between raw shot volume and shot quality allowed that conditions how corner-kick generation relates to actual goal threat.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) across two teams simultaneously, then relating that joint state to a third observable (corner kicks) and a fourth (goals). It cannot be reduced to any single observable against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession FOR (ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5) and their shots-on-target-to-shots ratio (derived from FOR observables), then examine the corner-kick FOR differential and goals FOR differential across matches where possession dominance and shot-quality ratio diverge between the two sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds higher possession but its shots-on-target-to-shots ratio is lower than the opponent's, its corner-kick generation rises relative to goals scored — the relationship between possession dominance and goal output is suppressed when shot quality is low.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The ratio of shots-on-target FOR to total shots FOR (conversion to on-target) differs asymmetrically between Team A and Team B, and this asymmetry interacts with each team's possession level to predict corner-kick differential — teams with higher possession but lower shot-quality ratios generate more corners without proportionally more goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, shots, shots-on-target) for both teams simultaneously, forming a ratio and interacting it with a second observable dimension. Not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team's fouls FOR RECENT_5 diverges downward from its ALL_PRIOR baseline while the opponent's fouls FOR RECENT_5 diverges upward from its ALL_PRIOR baseline. Within this asymmetric regime, measure whether cards_2h FOR and AGAINST are elevated relative to competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the two teams' recent foul trajectories diverge in opposite directions (one falling, one rising), second-half card volume rises above what either team's individual foul baseline predicts — the asymmetric divergence amplifies disciplinary outcomes in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate FOR has dropped sharply in recent form relative to its all-prior baseline, while Team B's foul rate FOR has risen in recent form — this asymmetric recent-vs-baseline divergence in fouls across the two teams jointly conditions the second-half card (cards_2h) volume, beyond what either team's foul rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint, asymmetric relationship across two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) for both teams simultaneously, conditioning on the direction of recent-vs-baseline divergence for each team independently and then combining them. It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Use first-half and second-half corner-kick FOR averages for each team alongside first-half and second-half goals AGAINST averages to identify whether the team that concentrates corners in the second half also concedes more goals in the second half, and whether this joint half-level pattern predicts total corner volume above competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's second-half corner share is structurally higher than its first-half share AND the opponent concedes more goals in the second half than the first half, total match corner volume rises above competition context — the half-level concentration of attacking pressure compounds with defensive vulnerability timing.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of corner kicks (first-half vs second-half) differs structurally between Team A and Team B: Team A generates a higher share of corners in the second half relative to the first half, while Team B's corner distribution across halves is more balanced. This half-level asymmetry in corner timing interacts with each team's goals-against first-half vs second-half split to condition total match corner volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first-half vs second-half) for two distinct observables (corners and goals) across both teams simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint half-resolution relationship across two observables and two teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B holds higher possession FOR than Team A (both all-prior and recent) but also concedes more goals AGAINST than Team A. Within this joint condition, examine whether offsides AGAINST (opponent offsides caught) are elevated for the high-possession but high-conceding team, indicating a high defensive line that is both a source of possession and a vulnerability.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds higher possession than its opponent but concedes goals at a higher rate, its offsides AGAINST (trapping opponents offside) rises above competition context — the high defensive line that enables possession also creates more offside traps but does not fully suppress goals conceded, and this joint pattern is detectable across matches.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession FOR is structurally above competition context and above Team A's possession FOR, yet Team B's goals AGAINST (both all-prior and recent) are substantially higher than Team A's goals AGAINST — indicating that possession dominance does not suppress goals conceded for Team B. Jointly conditioning on possession differential and goals-against differential across both teams reveals whether high-possession teams that still concede heavily also generate elevated offside counts (as a proxy for high defensive lines being exploited).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, goals, offsides) across both teams, conditioning on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (possession differential and goals-against differential). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.
